title: RAID5 one missing member
content: On the fictional ArcNAS system, RAID5 with exactly one failed drive is degraded. The support procedure is to verify the backup, identify the failed bay and replace that member before starting repair. Do not remove another healthy member or create a new pool.

title: RAID5 one missing member
content: Thank you for the screenshot showing one failed RAID5 member. Please confirm your backup and the failed bay number before we discuss replacement. Leave the remaining drives installed; this is not a request to initialize a new pool.

title: RAID5 two missing members
content: ArcNAS RAID5 with two unavailable members is beyond single-drive redundancy. Stop writes and escalate for recovery assessment; do not use the routine one-drive repair workflow. Preserve bay order and collect the failure sequence.

title: RAID5 two missing members
content: I understand that two disks disappeared from your RAID5 array. Please stop writes and keep the drives in their original bays. We will collect the failure timeline and arrange a recovery assessment instead of giving routine rebuild steps.

title: Pending sectors on a drive
content: Increasing pending or uncorrectable sector counts indicate a possible media problem. ArcNAS support asks for a verified backup, the drive serial and the trend in these counters. A passed quick test does not erase the warning.

title: Pending sectors on a drive
content: Thanks for sending the disk report. Because pending sectors are rising, please confirm your backup and send the drive serial plus the previous and current counts. A short test passing does not dismiss this warning.

title: Interface CRC counter
content: A growing interface CRC counter with stable media counters points first to the drive connection path. ArcNAS support checks the bay connection during an approved maintenance window and watches whether CRC errors continue. CRC counts alone do not prove damaged platter sectors.

title: Interface CRC counter
content: Thank you for the CRC report. Please send the counter trend and bay number so we can check the connection path during maintenance. We should not label the drive media defective from the CRC count alone.

title: SMB access denied for one user
content: If one account can log into the ArcNAS web console but cannot open an SMB share that other accounts can use, inspect that account's effective share permissions and group deny rules. Web login permission does not grant file access.

title: SMB access denied for one user
content: I see that your web login works while this share rejects your account. Please send the affected username and the share permission view, and tell us whether another account can open the same share. Do not grant Everyone full control as a workaround.

title: Windows cached SMB credentials
content: If Windows says multiple connections to a server using different usernames are not allowed, inspect existing SMB sessions and cached credentials for that server. This credential conflict occurs before share authorization; changing share ACLs is not the first step.

title: Windows cached SMB credentials
content: Thanks for the exact multiple-connections message. Please list existing sessions to that NAS and the account already in use. We will resolve the credential conflict before considering changes to share permissions.

title: NAS address changed after router replacement
content: When ArcNAS becomes unreachable at its old IP after replacing a DHCP router, check the new lease table, link lights and client subnet. A remembered address can be stale while the NAS is healthy. Do not reset storage to repair addressing.

title: NAS address changed after router replacement
content: Thanks for explaining that the router was replaced. Please send the new router's lease entry and your computer's IP range, and check the NAS link light. Keep storage settings unchanged while we locate its current address.

title: NAS name fails but IP works
content: When the ArcNAS web interface opens by IP but not by hostname, investigate DNS resolution and stale name records. Working access by IP distinguishes this from a failed network link. Storage initialization and disk replacement do not fix name resolution.

title: NAS name fails but IP works
content: Thank you for checking both addresses. Since the IP opens but the name does not, please send the hostname and the DNS result from your computer. We will investigate name resolution rather than change storage configuration.

title: Recovering one deleted file
content: ArcNAS file recovery from an existing snapshot requires the shared folder, file path and a recovery point before deletion. Restore only that file when the customer requests one document; a whole-folder rollback can overwrite unrelated newer files.

title: Recovering one deleted file
content: Sorry that the document was deleted. Please provide its path and the approximate deletion time so we can locate a snapshot from before the deletion. We will confirm a file-only recovery instead of rolling back the entire folder.

title: Snapshots retaining deleted blocks
content: Deleting live files may not free ArcNAS volume space while snapshots retain those blocks. Inspect snapshot retention and expected expiration before deleting recovery points. A restore operation does not release retained blocks.

title: Snapshots retaining deleted blocks
content: Thanks for the capacity screenshot. Please send the snapshot retention list and the time of the large deletion. We will explain which retained versions consume space before asking you to remove any recovery points.

title: Backup destination authentication failed
content: Backup error BK-401 on ArcNAS means the destination rejected authentication. Check the configured destination account and whether its secret expired. This code is distinct from BK-507 capacity exhaustion; deleting backup versions is not the authentication fix.

title: Backup destination authentication failed
content: Thank you for the BK-401 log. Please confirm whether the destination account or secret changed and send the job's destination name. Do not email us the password; we will verify the credential configuration with you.

title: Backup destination capacity exhausted
content: Backup error BK-507 on ArcNAS means the destination lacks room for the next backup. Review destination quota, free capacity and retention policy. Rotating the account password does not resolve this condition.

title: Backup destination capacity exhausted
content: Thanks for the BK-507 report. Please send the target's free capacity, quota and retention settings. We will agree on a capacity or retention change before removing old recovery versions.

title: A210 memory servicing policy
content: The fictional ArcNAS A210 has soldered memory and no supported memory expansion slot. Support must verify the exact model before recommending upgrades. The similar-looking A210+ has a different memory servicing policy.

title: A210 memory servicing policy
content: Thank you for asking about more memory. Your label identifies an A210 without the plus suffix; this model has no supported memory expansion slot. We can review workload settings, but should not send A210+ upgrade instructions.

title: A210+ memory servicing policy
content: The fictional ArcNAS A210+ supports one approved memory expansion module. Confirm the plus suffix and the module compatibility list before installation during shutdown. This procedure does not apply to the A210 base model.

title: A210+ memory servicing policy
content: Thanks for confirming the A210+ label. Please send the proposed module part number so we can check the compatibility list and plan a shutdown for installation. These instructions apply to the plus model only.

title: Lost second-factor device
content: For an ArcNAS user who knows the password but lost the authenticator, check available recovery codes and follow the verified administrator-assisted second-factor recovery process. Repeated password changes do not replace the missing second factor.

title: Lost second-factor device
content: I understand your phone is unavailable even though you know the password. Please confirm whether you still have recovery codes; otherwise we will use the verified administrator-assisted second-factor recovery process. Do not send us a recovery code.

title: Account locked after failed passwords
content: ArcNAS temporarily locks an account after repeated incorrect password attempts. Verify the lockout event and follow the unlock policy with the administrator. This is different from a missing authenticator device; disabling MFA is not the unlock procedure.

title: Account locked after failed passwords
content: Thank you for the lockout message. Please stop repeated sign-in attempts and tell us when the failures began so the administrator can verify and unlock the account under policy. We do not need to disable second-factor protection.

title: NFS root mapped to anonymous
content: On an ArcNAS NFS export, root squashing maps client root to an anonymous identity. If ordinary file owners can write but client root cannot, inspect export squash settings and intended UID mapping. This differs from a subnet being denied access to the export.

title: NFS root mapped to anonymous
content: Thanks for confirming ordinary users can write. Please send the export's squash setting and the relevant UID mapping. We will check why client root is mapped anonymously before changing export access networks.

title: NFS export denies a new subnet
content: An ArcNAS NFS mount rejected only after clients move to a new subnet should be checked against the export's allowed host or network list. If the mount itself is denied, root identity mapping is not yet the primary issue.

title: NFS export denies a new subnet
content: Thank you for noting the VLAN move. Please send the client's new address and the export's allowed network list. We will check mount access for that subnet before investigating permissions inside the mounted folder.

title: iSCSI CHAP negotiation failure
content: An ArcNAS iSCSI initiator that fails CHAP authentication before a session is established requires matching initiator and target authentication settings. Filesystem repair and LUN expansion are unrelated to this login stage.

title: iSCSI CHAP negotiation failure
content: Thanks for the CHAP negotiation error. Please send the initiator identifier and the authentication mode configured at each end, excluding secrets. We will correct session authentication before discussing LUN contents.

title: Connected iSCSI session without visible LUN
content: When an ArcNAS iSCSI session is established but no disk appears, check whether the LUN is mapped to that target and permitted for the initiator. Successful session login makes a CHAP password mismatch less likely.

title: Connected iSCSI session without visible LUN
content: Thank you for confirming the iSCSI session is connected. Please send the target-to-LUN mapping and the initiator access entry. We will check presentation of the disk before changing working authentication settings.

title: User quota reached
content: ArcNAS can deny one user's writes when that user's quota is full even if the volume has free space and other users can write. Inspect the account quota and ownership totals before adding disks.

title: User quota reached
content: Thanks for checking that other users can still save files. Please send your account's quota and usage, along with the affected folder. We will review the individual limit before proposing more storage hardware.

title: Volume capacity reached
content: When an ArcNAS volume is full, writes can fail for all accounts regardless of their personal quota. Review volume usage and safe capacity recovery options. Increasing a single account's quota does not create physical free space.

title: Volume capacity reached
content: Thank you for confirming all accounts are affected. Please send the volume usage view and recent growth details. We will assess capacity recovery before changing individual account limits.

title: TLS hostname mismatch
content: A browser certificate name warning on ArcNAS occurs when the address used is not covered by the certificate's names. Use the intended covered hostname or provision the correct certificate. A still-valid expiry date does not resolve a name mismatch.

title: TLS hostname mismatch
content: Thanks for the certificate warning. Please send the address you entered and the certificate names, without private keys. We will compare them rather than assume the certificate expired.

title: TLS certificate expired
content: An ArcNAS certificate whose validity period has ended must be renewed and the renewed certificate assigned to the intended service. The hostname may already match correctly. Changing DNS alone does not renew an expired certificate.

title: TLS certificate expired
content: Thank you for the expiry warning. Please send the certificate validity dates and the service using it. We will verify renewal and assignment; changing a correct hostname is not the renewal process.

title: Remote hostname points to an old public address
content: If ArcNAS remote access works using the current public IP but not its dynamic hostname, compare the hostname's DNS result with the router's current WAN address. Refresh stale dynamic DNS records rather than recreate internal shares.

title: Remote hostname points to an old public address
content: Thanks for testing the current public IP. Please send the dynamic hostname's resolved address and the router's WAN address. We will check whether the published record is stale.

title: Inbound access behind carrier NAT
content: An ArcNAS router WAN address inside 100.64.0.0/10 can indicate carrier-grade NAT. Local port forwarding alone cannot establish inbound reachability through the carrier's translation. Confirm the addressing arrangement with the provider or use an approved relay.

title: Inbound access behind carrier NAT
content: Thank you for the WAN details. Since the router shows a shared carrier address, please confirm inbound connectivity options with your provider. Repeatedly adding the same port-forward rule is unlikely to address the upstream translation.

title: Two-way sync propagates deletion
content: In ArcNAS two-way folder synchronization, a deletion can propagate to the peer. Pause the affected task and inspect its event history before restoring files. Synchronization is not an independent retained backup.

title: Two-way sync propagates deletion
content: I am sorry the deletion appeared on both sides. Please pause this two-way task and send its event history so we can identify the deletion source before recovery. We should not describe synchronization as a retained backup.

title: Concurrent edits create a sync conflict
content: When both sides edit the same ArcNAS synchronized file before synchronization completes, conflict copies preserve competing versions. Compare both versions with their owners before selecting one. Do not delete a conflict copy solely because its filename looks redundant.

title: Concurrent edits create a sync conflict
content: Thanks for reporting both versions. Please keep the conflict copy and the original, and tell us who edited each side and when. We will compare the contents with the owners before deciding which version to retain.

title: SATA disk compatibility
content: The fictional ArcNAS A420 drive bays accept approved SATA drives and do not support SAS drives even when their physical size is similar. Check the interface and exact compatibility entry before purchasing a replacement.

title: SATA disk compatibility
content: Thanks for sending the replacement listing. Please confirm its interface and part number; an A420 requires an approved SATA drive. A physically similar SAS drive should not be ordered for these bays.

title: NVMe cache is not a bay replacement
content: The fictional ArcNAS A420 M.2 sockets accept supported NVMe cache modules. An NVMe module is not a replacement member for a failed SATA drive-bay array. Verify the failed component type before selecting a part.

title: NVMe cache is not a bay replacement
content: Thank you for the part suggestion. Please send the failed bay or slot identifier. If a SATA array member failed, an NVMe cache module cannot replace that member even though the appliance has M.2 sockets.

title: UPS battery takeover
content: When ArcNAS receives a UPS on-battery event during a mains outage, verify estimated runtime and the configured safe shutdown policy. Do not treat loss of mains as merely a monitoring cable issue if the UPS confirms battery operation.

title: UPS battery takeover
content: Thank you for reporting the power outage. Please send the UPS remaining runtime and shutdown policy so we can confirm a controlled shutdown before battery exhaustion. Avoid running long storage maintenance on battery power.

title: UPS monitoring connection lost
content: When ArcNAS reports loss of UPS communication while mains power remains normal, inspect the USB or network monitoring path and supported UPS settings. A communication alert alone does not prove the battery is discharging.

title: UPS monitoring connection lost
content: Thanks for checking that mains power is present. Please send the UPS display status and the monitoring connection type so we can inspect the communication path. We should not report a confirmed power outage from this alert alone.

title: Firmware update during array repair
content: ArcNAS support defers elective firmware upgrades while an array repair is running. Wait for repair completion and verify backup and array health before scheduling the update. A firmware update is not a way to accelerate repair.

title: Firmware update during array repair
content: Thank you for checking before updating. Please let the active repair finish, then send the array health and backup status so we can schedule the firmware upgrade. Installing it now is not a repair-speed remedy.

title: Firmware package signature rejected
content: If ArcNAS rejects an update package signature, verify the exact model, package source and checksum. Do not disable signature verification or retry a package for a similar model. This check is independent of array repair scheduling.

title: Firmware package signature rejected
content: Thanks for the signature error. Please send the exact model and the package download source and checksum. We will verify the correct signed package instead of asking you to bypass signature checks.

title: SMTP connection timeout
content: ArcNAS notification delivery that times out before receiving an SMTP greeting requires checking server address, port and network egress. Password changes do not fix a connection that never reaches authentication.

title: SMTP connection timeout
content: Thanks for the timeout log. Please send the SMTP host, port and a connection test result, without credentials. We will confirm network reachability before investigating account authentication.

title: SMTP authentication rejected
content: An ArcNAS SMTP exchange that connects successfully but receives a 535 authentication rejection requires checking account authentication requirements and credentials. An open TCP port does not guarantee successful mail authentication.

title: SMTP authentication rejected
content: Thank you for the 535 response. Please confirm the account authentication method required by your mail provider and whether the configured credential changed. Do not send the credential itself.

title: Encrypted share needs its key
content: An ArcNAS encrypted share that remains locked after restart requires the correct share encryption key or configured key-management recovery path. An administrator login password is not a substitute for the encryption key. Do not create a replacement share over the existing data.

title: Encrypted share needs its key
content: I understand the share stayed locked after restart. Please confirm whether the saved encryption key or configured key manager is available, without sending the key to us. We cannot promise that an administrator password replaces it.

title: Unlocked encrypted share rejects one user
content: If an ArcNAS encrypted share is already mounted and other users can read it, one user's access denial should be investigated through permissions. Reimporting the encryption key is not the first step for a single-account authorization failure.

title: Unlocked encrypted share rejects one user
content: Thank you for confirming others can read the mounted encrypted folder. Please send the affected account and effective share permissions. We will inspect access rules before changing working encryption-key settings.

title: Read-only cache removal
content: The fictional ArcNAS read-only SSD cache contains cached copies rather than unique pending writes. Use the documented cache removal procedure and confirm its read-only mode before removing hardware. Do not apply this assumption to write-back cache.

title: Read-only cache removal
content: Thanks for planning the cache removal. Please send the cache mode and health view so we can confirm it is read-only and guide its documented removal. We must not assume that every cache mode has the same removal requirements.

title: Write-back cache removal
content: The fictional ArcNAS write-back SSD cache may contain writes not yet destaged to the volume. Follow the flush and safe-detach procedure before removing hardware. Treating it like a read-only cache risks losing pending writes.

title: Write-back cache removal
content: Thank you for checking before pulling the SSDs. Because this is write-back cache, please leave them installed until we verify successful flush and safe detach. We cannot reuse the read-only removal assumption.

title: NAS switch port in wrong VLAN
content: When ArcNAS loses network access immediately after a switch-port VLAN change, verify access or trunk mode, tagging and the intended subnet on that port. This differs from firewall blocking only one service while other NAS services work.

title: NAS switch port in wrong VLAN
content: Thanks for identifying the switch change. Please send the NAS port VLAN mode and intended network, and check link status. We will restore the expected network path before altering individual application rules.

title: One NAS service blocked
content: If ArcNAS file sharing works but the management HTTPS port is unreachable from a restricted subnet, inspect service-specific firewall rules and listening ports. A functioning file-sharing connection means the entire network link is not down.

title: One NAS service blocked
content: Thank you for confirming file sharing still works. Please send the management port and the firewall rule for your source subnet. We will check that service's access rule rather than assume the NAS link is disconnected.

title: Replication lag exceeds recovery objective
content: ArcNAS snapshot replication that succeeds but trails the recovery objective requires checking schedule, transfer duration and changed-data volume. A healthy task can still leave a larger recovery gap than the agreed objective.

title: Replication lag exceeds recovery objective
content: Thanks for confirming replication succeeds. Please send its last completed recovery point, schedule and transfer duration so we can compare the lag with your recovery objective. Success alone does not establish that the recovery gap is acceptable.

title: Replication destination unreachable
content: ArcNAS replication that cannot connect to the destination requires checking destination availability, route and replication service port. Increasing snapshot frequency does not restore a failed connection.

title: Replication destination unreachable
content: Thank you for the destination-unreachable log. Please send the destination status and a reachability check for the replication port. We will restore the connection before increasing the schedule frequency.

title: Data scrub detects checksum mismatch
content: An ArcNAS data scrub checks stored data integrity and reports checksum inconsistencies. Investigate affected files and redundancy health when mismatches appear. A scrub result is not a measure of how evenly capacity is allocated across drives.

title: Data scrub detects checksum mismatch
content: Thanks for the checksum report. Please send the affected file list and array health so we can investigate integrity and available recovery copies. We will not treat this as a capacity-balancing notification.

title: Capacity redistribution after expansion
content: The fictional ArcNAS redistribution task after pool expansion moves data to use added capacity. It is distinct from a checksum scrub and does not certify every file's integrity. Review redistribution progress separately from integrity alerts.

title: Capacity redistribution after expansion
content: Thank you for the expansion progress report. Please send the redistribution status so we can check use of the added capacity. Completion of this task alone should not be presented as proof that every file passed an integrity check.

title: Standard outage escalation
content: Under the fictional ArcNAS Standard support policy, an outage is triaged in the business-hours queue. Record affected users, start time and available diagnostics; do not promise the Premium 24-hour callback entitlement.

title: Standard outage escalation
content: I am sorry your team cannot access the NAS. Please send the outage start time and number of affected users so we can prioritize the Standard business-hours queue. We should not promise a Premium callback entitlement on this plan.

title: Premium outage escalation
content: Under the fictional ArcNAS Premium support policy, a verified service-wide outage qualifies for the round-the-clock incident callback queue. Record the contract identifier, impact and callback contact through the approved channel. Standard-plan timing does not apply.

title: Premium outage escalation
content: I understand this outage is affecting your whole team. Please provide the Premium contract identifier and approved callback contact so we can open the round-the-clock incident escalation. We will record impact before discussing optional features.

title: Diagnostic bundle privacy review
content: Before attaching ArcNAS diagnostics to a support case, review the bundle for credentials, tokens and personal data under the approved redaction process. Preserve useful timestamps and error identifiers where possible. Do not paste secrets into email.

title: Diagnostic bundle privacy review
content: Thank you for preparing diagnostics. Please use the approved review and redaction process before uploading the bundle through the support channel. Keep timestamps and error identifiers useful, but do not send passwords or tokens in email.

title: Diagnostic capture time window
content: For intermittent ArcNAS faults, collect diagnostics covering the incident time with timezone and a short surrounding interval. A bundle containing only the next day's healthy state may miss the failure. Record when the symptom occurred before exporting logs.

title: Diagnostic capture time window
content: Thanks for the intermittent-failure report. Please tell us the incident time and timezone, then export the surrounding log interval. A capture of today's healthy state alone may not explain yesterday's interruption.

title: File search index stale
content: When an ArcNAS file is visible by browsing but absent from search, inspect indexing scope, exclusions and index status. This symptom does not by itself indicate the file is deleted or require snapshot recovery.

title: File search index stale
content: Thank you for confirming the file opens when browsing. Please send its folder path and indexing status so we can check whether it is included and indexed. We should not start deleted-file recovery for a file that still exists.

title: Search visibility follows user permissions
content: ArcNAS search filters results using the requesting user's access permissions. If one user finds a file and another cannot access its folder, inspect access rules before rebuilding the index. A common index can yield different visible results per account.

title: Search visibility follows user permissions
content: Thanks for comparing both accounts. Please send the affected user's folder access and the account that can find the file. We will check permission-filtered visibility before scheduling a full reindex.
